newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settler arrested for West Bank shooting.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settler arrested for West Bank shooting.

text.p: Israeli police on Monday arrested a Jewish settler from the West Bank as a suspect in the shooting of a Palestinian at the village of Kharbatha earlier in the day, a police spokeswoman said.
The new West Bank violence coincided with a crisis visit to Washington by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu who met U.S. President Bill Clinton for talks to save faltering Middle East peace efforts.

"After an intense investigation and in cooperation with Palestinian police, investigators from the Benyamin station arrested a suspect in the shooting this morning at Kharbatha," the spokeswoman said.

One Palestinian was in serious condition at the West Bank's Ramallah hospital with a gunshot wound to the chest. Initially two people were reported shot but police said later one hurt himself falling while trying to help the man who was shot.
Police described the suspect as a resident of a Jewish settlement which they didn't name.

"(He is) a resident of one of the settlements near the village (Kharbatha), is 44 years old, married with five children," a police announcement said. They said they found his car and an M-16 assault rifle.
Palestinian witnesses said a Jewish settler fired on students and others in Kharbatha village, 17 kms (11 miles) west of Ramallah. Two Arabs were treated in hospital, one with a gunshot wound.
Israeli police said before the arrest the gunman opened fire after Palestinians pelted his car with stones and then fled in the car.

But villagers said the settler appeared to be looking for a confrontation. They said he had been deliberately driving near the school for some time even though the Israeli government had built a bypass road for Jews in the area.
The Palestinian Authority, which controls eight West Bank towns including Ramallah, administers Kharbatha. But the village is under full Israeli security jurisdiction.

The West Bank and Gaza have been rocked by unrest since Israel broke ground on March 18 for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. Three Palestinians have been killed by Israeli gunfire and scores of people wounded.
"A settler got out of his car and began to shoot...The students ran away and after that the settler himself...began to fire in the air and randomly," a Palestinian witness said.
"After that he shot two people from our village, one to his chest, and his case is not very good," he said.
A Jewish settler spokesman said the man opened fire in response to "massive stone-throwing".
But Khaled Injas, of Kharbatha, said: "I don't know why he comes to this village every day. They have their own road."
Some 130,000 Jews live in settlements scattered among more than two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza, areas captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
